stimulus.text:
“That all persons within the jurisdiction of the United States shall be entitled to the full and equal enjoyment of the accommodations, advantages, facilities, and privileges of inns, public conveyances on land or water, theaters, and other places of public amusement; subject only to the conditions and limitations established by law, and applicable alike to citizens of every race and color, regardless of any previous condition of servitude.”

—Civil Rights Act of 1875, Section 1 (March 1, 1875)

rationales.A: Congress passed the act and the Court struck it down; the two branches pulled apart.
rationales.B: Background: Congress wrote and passed the act; the Court judged it.
rationales.C: Background: the amendments were never repealed; they were narrowed and left unenforced.
rationales.D: Congress kept reaching for new protections as late as 1875, while the Court kept narrowing them: Slaughter-House in 1873, Cruikshank in 1876, the Civil Rights Cases in 1883. The laws were written, then the courts took their force away.
rationales.general:
1. The act itself is Congress reaching for protection as late as 1875.
2. Background: the Court had already narrowed the amendments in Slaughter-House and Cruikshank.
3. In 1883 the Court finished the pattern by striking the act down.
4. Two branches, two directions: one writing protections, one removing them.
Remember: a reform can be defeated without a single repeal, one court decision at a time.
